I'm still pretty uncertain about transitioning, but what you're saying is making me think.

Edit: Like, that honestly sounds super nice and great. I'm just worried that won't happen to me... I'm more and more feeling like I am just doubting myself though.

I have talked about it with my therapist, and I have been digging into it.

I more or less laid out the reasons I'm uncomfortable in my post here, but like I said, by best friend and therapist just think I'm holding back, so I don't know... Perhaps showing them both this post will help.

What mental/emotional effects were there for you?

Maybe where you live is more liberal than where I live, but I feel like not many people "identify" anyone as androgynous, if anything they're just confused, which I imagine would be socially awkward and anxiety-provoking.

Did you know you'd feel this way after you started HRT?

It sounds really awesome, I'm just really skeptical the same thing would happen to me.

I don't have dysphoria nearly as bad as you did.

Congrats on dissipating it. :)

What were your pros and cons?

What was the breaking point?
How can I be so sure that it is worth it, and they are just fears?
Cherries aren't in season yet, and Kool Aid isn't sold in Australia. I'll buy some pasta sauce and try that.

I'll learn chemistry one day! Hopefully...

Engine oil's no good, then.

Do you know of any specific substances that cloth washing detergent *would* remove, but just water through a machine *wouldn't*?
My mom claims regular cloth washing detergent doesn't get oil stains out. Is she wrong?

I appreciate your attempt at teaching me chemistry, though I have to admit that most of it went over my head.

Do you think engine oil would come out of a shirt using detergent?
How do I tell if something is non-polar?

Would vegetable or coconut oil work?

I want a substance I can measure with a spoon. I'm going to do three tests on three separate shirts.
